title: Alex Blania on Proof of Human and Building World's Identity Network

reader_summary.headline: Alex Blania explains how to prove you are human against AI fakes.
reader_summary.overview: AI agents can now trick people into thinking they are real humans online. Old ID methods fail because they cannot prove a person is unique among billions. Alex Blania describes a new system using eye scans and privacy tools to solve this problem.

key_points.text: AI agents can fool humans into thinking they are real people, making it hard to tell who is human online.
key_points.evidence_quote: The AIs are really good at programming humans. Much better than humans are programming AIs. Absolutely. They will be able to have a good account and will be able to post and also test to five other AIs that these are in fact humans and even though they're not.

key_points.text: The system splits iris data into pieces sent to multiple computers so no single server holds your full biometric information.
key_points.evidence_quote: we take a picture of the iris, we calculate an iris code, then we break that iris code in multiple pieces and send it to multiple computers such that there is no central database in some sort.

key_points.text: Zero-knowledge proofs let you prove you are a unique human to a platform without revealing your identity or biometric data.
key_points.evidence_quote: we separate all of this from you with a zero-knowledge proof. So meaning you have to secret on your phone, but no one else has it.

key_points.text: Dating apps like Tinder will use this to show users they are real humans, not bots, and verify their true identity.
key_points.evidence_quote: if you verified with an orb, you get a little batch that signals to other people that you are, in fact, humans with a high level of verification.

notes: a16z's Ben Horowitz and Erik Torenberg speak with Alex Blania, cofounder and CEO of Tools for Humanity, World, and cofounder of Merge Labs. World is building the largest real human network, a proof-of-human layer for the AI era. They cover the technical challenge of proving human uniqueness at scale using iris biometrics, the privacy architecture behind World ID, and why platforms from social networks to dating apps to video conferencing will soon require proof of human verification.
